## The one line that changes, and the three that must not
All generatedAt sites live in scripts/roadmap/render.ts (no cli.ts — main() is in the same file):
- render.ts:275 `<time datetime="${escapeHtml(generatedAt)}">${escapeHtml(generatedAt)}</time>` — ONLY the text-content half changes to the local rendering. datetime attr keeps ISO.
- render.ts:302 `new Date().toISOString()` in main() — the ONLY clock call; stays the only one. The display string is formatted FROM generatedAt.
- buildStamp (:90-92, identity) + stamp.txt write (:310) — unchanged, ISO.
- REFRESH_SCRIPT CURRENT (:191-192, JSON.stringify(stamp)) — unchanged, ISO; it compares against stamp.txt.

## TRAP — the two lookalike specs stay green and stay UNTOUCHED
cli.spec.ts:49-57 (`toContain(stamp)` — ISO survives in the datetime attr) and render.spec.ts:587-590 (happy-dom textContent includes <script> source, so the ISO inside REFRESH_SCRIPT keeps it green) both still pass after the fix. They correctly guard machine identity — LEAVE THEM. The new pin must be NEW assertions:
- `doc.querySelector('time')?.getAttribute('datetime')` === the ISO instant, AND
- `doc.querySelector('time')?.textContent` === the exact local rendering — two different strings from one instant.

## Exact expected strings (research ran real Intl on Node 22.14.0 full-ICU; both dbs of truth agree)
- Format target: dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm + zone marker. NOTE: no dateStyle/timeStyle preset produces it — presets emit `10.09.2026, 06:33` (comma) or two-digit year; the implementation must assemble from formatToParts. Assert the SPACE (not comma) between date and time so a naive .format() fails.
- Zone marker: Intl timeZoneName 'shortOffset' for et-EE/Europe/Tallinn yields `GMT +3` summer / `GMT +2` winter — WITH a space after GMT. Keep Intl's native spacing (stated choice).
- DST BOTH SIDES (the issue's hard requirement): instant 2026-07-01T12:00:00Z → `01.07.2026 15:00 GMT +3`; instant 2026-01-15T12:00:00Z → `15.01.2026 14:00 GMT +2`. A hardcoded +03:00 renders the January instant 15:00 — the test must catch exactly that.
- Milliseconds gone from the visible text; ISO keeps them.

## Also pin
- Self-refresh unaffected: REFRESH_SCRIPT still embeds the ISO stamp and still compares against stamp.txt content (existing specs mostly cover; add nothing that weakens them).
- 'Generated at' stays English.

tasks.commitBody: The board's generated-at stamp now reads as Estonian wall-clock time — 10.09.2026 06:33 GMT +3 — instead of a raw UTC ISO string with milliseconds. One instant, rendered twice: the machine identity is untouched, so stamp.txt, the time element's datetime attribute and the refresh script's compare value all still carry the exact ISO instant, and only the text a human reads is formatted, from that same value, never from a second clock call. The zone is applied as IANA Europe/Tallinn through Intl, not a numeric offset, so the display flips to GMT +2 in late October with no code change — and a test pins an instant on each side of that boundary, because a hardcoded offset would ship correct today and go silently wrong for half the year. The string is assembled from formatToParts: no locale preset produces the plain date-space-time shape, and the assembly is what lets the tests assert the full string strictly. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills>.
